cases.translation: There is nothing alcoholic, said the bouncer.
cases.explain: The word is the subject of «сказал», so it stands in the nominative; вышибала looks feminine but is a masculine noun of the first declension.

cases.translation: There is udder, but there is no sherry!
cases.explain: «Нет» expressing absence requires the genitive; with mass nouns like херес Russian often uses the old partitive genitive ending -у instead of -а.

cases.sentence: Прижал его к ___ в ожидании заказа.
cases.translation: He pressed it to his heart while waiting for his order.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (towards, up against) always governs the dative: к сердцу.

cases.translation: I set about examining the chandelier over my head.
cases.explain: Люстра is the direct object of «рассматривать», and a direct object without negation takes the accusative.

cases.sentence: Я вслед этой женщине посмотрел с ___.
cases.translation: I looked after that woman with disgust.
cases.explain: «С» describing the manner or accompanying feeling of an action governs the instrumental: с отвращением.

cases.sentence: И в их ___ отразилась эта смутность.
cases.translation: And that same murkiness was reflected in their eyes too.
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (a location, not a direction) takes the prepositional; the plural ending here is -ах.

cases.sentence: Я ведь просто еду в ___, к любимой девушке.
cases.translation: I am simply going to Petushki, to the girl I love.
cases.explain: «В» with a verb of motion answering «куда?» takes the accusative; Петушки is an inanimate plural, so its accusative is identical to the nominative.

cases.translation: White stockings without any seam at all.
cases.explain: The preposition «без» (here in its fuller form «безо») always governs the genitive; the о of шов drops out in the oblique cases.

reading.question: What is Venichka told when he comes into the Kursk station restaurant?
options: That there is nothing alcoholic to be had
That the restaurant is closed for the night
That he must first buy a train ticket
reading.correct: That there is nothing alcoholic to be had
reading.explain: The bouncer's words «Спиртного ничего нет» are the blow the whole chapter turns on.

reading.ru: И оглядел меня всего, как дохлую птичку или как грязный лютик.
reading.question: How does the bouncer look Venichka over?
options: As if he were a dead little bird or a dirty buttercup
As if he were an old friend
reading.correct: As if he were a dead little bird or a dirty buttercup
reading.explain: The comparison to a dead bird and a dirty buttercup sets the tone of how the staff treat him.

reading.ru: Чемоданчик я все-таки взял с собой и, как давеча в подъезде, прижал его к сердцу в ожидании заказа.
reading.question: What does Venichka do with his little suitcase while he waits for his order?
options: He presses it to his heart, as he had done earlier in the entrance hall
He leaves it with the cloakroom attendant
He puts it down by the door
He opens it and starts eating the presents
reading.correct: He presses it to his heart, as he had done earlier in the entrance hall
reading.explain: He keeps the suitcase of presents clutched to his chest exactly as he had in the doorway that morning.

reading.ru: Ведь если верить ангелам, здесь не переводился херес.
reading.question: What had the angels led Venichka to expect of this restaurant?
options: That sherry was never in short supply there
That the food would be free
That he would meet his beloved there
That the place would be empty at that hour
reading.correct: That sherry was never in short supply there
reading.explain: He recalls the angels' promise that sherry never ran out at the Kursk station restaurant.

reading.ru: Это ведь и в самом деле Иван Козловский поет, я сразу узнал, мерзее этого голоса нет.
reading.question: Whose singing does Venichka hear in the restaurant?
options: A drunk at the next table's
reading.explain: He recognises Kozlovsky at once and declares there is no more loathsome voice.

reading.ru: Все голоса у всех певцов одинаково мерзкие, но мерзкие у каждого по-своему.
reading.question: What general claim does Venichka make about singers' voices?
options: They are all equally loathsome, but each in its own way
They are all beautiful in the same way
He cannot tell one from another
reading.correct: They are all equally loathsome, but each in its own way
reading.explain: This is why, he says, he can tell singers apart so easily by ear.

reading.question: How does Venichka react when the waitress lists udder among the dishes?
reading.explain: The mention of вымя brings back the sickness he is trying to hold down.

reading.question: What contrast does Venichka find so remarkable in the restaurant's offerings?
options: There is udder but no sherry
There is sherry but no food
There is music but no waiters
There is beer but no vodka
reading.correct: There is udder but no sherry
reading.explain: He is struck that the kitchen can offer udder while the bar has no sherry at all.

reading.ru: Тяжелая это мысль: ты сидишь, а на тебя сверху люстра.
reading.question: What does Venichka start imagining as he stares at the ceiling?
options: That the heavy chandelier comes down on him while he sits there
That the train leaves without him
That the angels come down to him
reading.correct: That the heavy chandelier comes down on him while he sits there
reading.explain: He works the falling chandelier into a whole meditation on how heavy a thought it is.

reading.ru: Сказано же тебе русским языком: нет у нас хереса!
reading.question: How does the waitress answer when Venichka finally orders 800 grams of sherry?
options: She snaps that he has been told plainly there is no sherry
She asks him to pay in advance
reading.correct: She snaps that he has been told plainly there is no sherry
reading.explain: She tells him it has been said to him in plain Russian that they have no sherry.

reading.ru: Я вслед этой женщине посмотрел с отвращением.
reading.question: How does Venichka watch the waitress as she walks away?
options: With disgust, especially at her seamless white stockings
Without lifting his eyes at all
With hope that she will change her mind
reading.correct: With disgust, especially at her seamless white stockings
reading.explain: He says a seam on the stockings might have humbled him and relieved his soul.

reading.question: What does Venichka ask himself about the restaurant staff?
options: Why they are all so rude, precisely when one must not be rude
Why they work such long hours
Why they never listen to music
Why they are all dressed in white
reading.correct: Why they are all so rude, precisely when one must not be rude
reading.explain: He complains they are pointedly rude just when a hungover man's nerves are laid bare.

reading.ru: «Всеобщее малодушие» – да ведь это спасение от всех бед, это панацея, это предикат величайшего совершенства!
reading.question: What does Venichka call universal faint-heartedness?
options: Salvation from all woes, a panacea and the mark of the highest perfection
The worst of all human vices
A disease that only sherry can cure
reading.correct: Salvation from all woes, a panacea and the mark of the highest perfection
reading.explain: He dreams of a world with no enthusiasts and no heroic deeds, only universal faint-heartedness.

reading.ru: Надо мной – две женщины и один мужчина, все трое в белом.
reading.question: Who comes and stands over Venichka's table?
options: Two women and a man, all three dressed in white
reading.correct: Two women and a man, all three dressed in white
reading.explain: The three figures in white appear as a kind of tribunal above him.

reading.ru: Зря это я опять про херес, зря!
reading.question: What does Venichka immediately regret having done?
options: Bringing his suitcase into the restaurant
Saying he was going to Petushki
reading.explain: The word sherry sets the three of them off at once.

reading.ru: Следом за мной чемоданчик с гостинцами; тоже – вытолкнули.
reading.question: How does Venichka's time in the restaurant end?
options: He is dragged across the hall and shoved outside, with his suitcase thrown out after him
He pays his bill and leaves quietly
He falls asleep at the table
He is finally served his sherry
reading.correct: He is dragged across the hall and shoved outside, with his suitcase thrown out after him
reading.explain: All three take him under the arms, lead him the length of the hall and push him out, and the suitcase of presents follows.

highlight.question: Which sentence says in what order Venichka bought the nuts and the sweets?
sentences: Нет, только не между пивом и альб-де-дессертом, там уж решительно не было никакой паузы.
А вот до кориандровой – это очень может быть.
Скорее даже так: орехи я купил до кориандровой, а уж конфеты – после.
А может быть и наоборот: выпив кориандровой, я…
highlight.explain: Only the third sentence actually puts the nuts before the coriander vodka and the sweets after it.

highlight.question: Which sentence names the pretext Venichka invents for coming in — what he says he wants to eat and listen to?
sentences: Я, хоть весь и сжался от отчаяния, но все-таки сумел промямлить, что пришел вовсе не за этим.
Мало ли зачем я пришел?
Может быть, мой экспресс на Пермь по какой-то причине не хочет идти на Пермь, и вот я сюда пришел: съесть бефстроганов и послушать Ивана Козловского или что-нибудь из «Цирюльника».
highlight.explain: The last sentence supplies the invented reason: beef stroganoff and Ivan Kozlovsky.

highlight.question: Which sentence explains why being hit by the falling chandelier would not in fact hurt?
sentences: Хорошая люстра.
Но уж слишком тяжелая.
Если она сейчас сорвется и упадет кому-нибудь на голову, – будет страшно больно…
Да нет, наверно, даже и не больно: пока она срывается и летит, ты сидишь и, ничего не подозревая, пьешь, например, херес.
А как она до тебя долетела – тебя уже нет в живых.
Тяжелая это мысль: ты сидишь, а на тебя сверху люстра.
Очень тяжелая мысль…
highlight.explain: The fourth sentence reverses the previous one by pointing out that you sit there drinking, suspecting nothing, while it falls.

highlight.question: Which sentence names the detail of the waitress that Venichka found especially repellent?
sentences: И опять меня оставили.
Я вслед этой женщине посмотрел с отвращением.
В особенности на белые чулки безо всякого шва; шов бы меня смирил, может быть, разгрузил бы душу и совесть…
highlight.explain: The third sentence singles out her white stockings without a seam.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes the three people who suddenly stand over Venichka?
sentences: Надо мной – две женщины и один мужчина, все трое в белом.

Я поднял глаза на них – о, сколько, должно быть, в моих глазах сейчас всякого безобразия и смутности – я это понял по ним, по их глазам, потому что и в их глазах отразилась эта смутность и это безобразие…
Я весь как-то сник и растерял душу.
highlight.explain: The first sentence counts them and says all three are dressed in white.

highlight.question: Which sentence says what happened to the little suitcase with the presents?
sentences: Зря это я опять про херес, зря!
Он их сразу взорвал.
Все трое подхватили меня под руки и через весь зал – о, боль такого позора! – через весь зал провели меня и вытолкнули на воздух.
Следом за мной чемоданчик с гостинцами; тоже – вытолкнули.
highlight.explain: The last sentence reports that the suitcase was shoved out after him.
